Common questions

What is a Codex reset?

A Codex reset is a global or plan-scoped refresh of usage limits. It is different from a user’s normal rolling quota window.

Is a Codex reset global?

This monitor focuses on resets announced or observed across a broad group of Codex users, not an individual account’s routine recovery.

How does this monitor verify a Tibo reset announcement?

Tibo Sottiaux is one of the first-party sources this monitor checks. A post or reply counts as a confirmed Codex reset only when it explicitly describes a global or broad reset; hints, capacity updates, and personal quota timers remain unconfirmed signals.

Is a Codex usage reset the same as a weekly limit reset?

No. A Codex usage reset may describe a broad reset announced for many users, while a weekly limit reset is the scheduled recovery shown for an individual account. This monitor separates shared reset evidence from personal quota timing.

When will Codex reset again?

There is no guaranteed public schedule. GPT-5.6 estimates the rolling 24h and 48h probabilities from the last confirmed reset, reset history, public posts and replies, stated timing, and limited account telemetry.

How is the Codex reset Forecast Score calculated?

With no predictive X signal after the latest confirmed reset, the site uses the empirical 24h and 48h reset-cadence baseline. When new semantic evidence appears, GPT-5.6 reads its timing, scope, wording, reply context, history, and limited account telemetry, then adjusts the estimate from that baseline. The previous displayed probability is withheld to reduce anchoring. High-impact estimates receive an independent GPT review. Results remain experimental until enough resolved forecasts pass the published calibration gate.

Is this an official OpenAI website?

No. Codex Reset Monitor is an independent project that organizes public evidence and links back to every source.
